title: Domestic change without abrupt deprivation

captions.physics: Changing routines through a new understanding

meaning: Your domestic support preserves freedom when new understanding allows an ending’s cost to be discussed instead of requiring both to retain everything or abandon it in one move.
text: Recognising domestic workload may encourage different action without making the familiar immediately unimportant. Judgement in the physical position of Muladhara appears through changed actions following new understanding. Death in energy can close earlier possibilities too quickly. The Devil in emotions holds to familiar comfort. Both may understand change’s necessity and feel drawn back: an abrupt ending leaves too little room for the cost of relinquishing, while attachment starts defending even what clearly obstructs present life. Understanding and wanting are not automatically resolved together.

For example, you realise a huge supply of home entertainment takes much space. Removing everything immediately affects rarely used items and favourite games for evenings alike. **A considered ending allows specific choices instead of general deprivation.** Discussing actual use reveals what is valuable and burdensome separately. It promises no preservation of every pleasure but lets both acknowledge attachment without subordinating the entire new domestic routine to it.

The difficulty is answering resistance through an even sharper rejection or returning everything unchanged. New understanding disappears between two extremes. Support grows when both can name aim and cost. Change becomes more manageable when it ends what is specifically outdated rather than requiring readiness for another home to be proved through losing every familiar pleasant possibility that still helps life. The choice can be narrower than complete abandonment.
